cases.title: The Documents tab shows the exposed libraries
cases.preconditions: signed in; at least two exposed libraries on the site
steps: Open LeanBoard → Documents.
Read the tiles.
cases.expected: one tile per exposed library with its document count; the ingestion and template libraries are not register tiles; the tiles open the register scoped to that library

cases.title: Open a library and read the register
cases.preconditions: a library with more than 20 documents
steps: Open a library tile.
Scroll the list; use the "more" paging at the bottom.
cases.expected: the register lists the documents with Document, status chip, owner and the library's chosen columns; the header and the Document column stay in place while the rest scrolls sideways in a narrow window; paging loads more rows without losing the scroll position

cases.title: The status line counts and the timing readout
cases.preconditions: signed in as a super admin
steps: Open a library; watch the Document tasks button while the page loads.
Read the status line under the toolbar; hover it.
cases.expected: the Document tasks button reads "Document tasks · …" with a small spinner until the count arrives, then the count; "N documents of M" with "loaded in … · feed … · opened in …" for a super admin only; the tooltip lists every load with its trigger; a plain user sees the count alone

cases.title: Search by name
cases.preconditions: a library with a document whose name contains a distinctive word
steps: Type part of the name in the search box; press Enter.
Clear the search.
cases.expected: only matching documents remain, the count follows; clearing restores the full list

cases.title: Filter by status
cases.preconditions: a standards library with approved and draft documents
steps: With "Show only approved" ticked, open Filters → Status.
Click "Show every status"; tick Draft.
Tick Approved as well, then clear the filter.
cases.expected: under the approved-only default the Status group says the register shows approved documents only and offers "Show every status" instead of hiding; after it, each tick narrows or widens the list at once; the filter pill shows the chosen values; Clear all removes every filter

cases.title: Show only approved
cases.preconditions: a standards library with approved and non-approved documents
steps: Kebab ⋮ → read "✓ Show only approved" (ticked by default).
Untick it.
Tick it again.
cases.expected: a reader lands with it ticked; a document controller or super admin lands with it unticked (every status); ticked, the register hides drafts, superseded and obsolete documents and the Status group explains itself instead of filtering; a document that leaves the approved stage while ticked (superseded, obsoleted) drops from the list at once with a status line; unticked, every stage shows and Status can be filtered; the choice is remembered for the view

cases.title: Filter by organisation at a parent level
cases.preconditions: documents tagged with organisation terms under one parent (a site or department)
steps: Filters → Organisation → pick a parent term (a department with areas under it).
Open one of the results and read its Organisation value.
cases.expected: documents tagged anywhere beneath the parent appear, not only those tagged with the parent itself; the pill names the parent; on a browser that has never loaded the tree, the Folders pane paints the viewer's own site branch within a few seconds with "Loading the rest of the organisation…" above it, and the other sites fill in behind "Show other sites" as the walk completes

cases.title: Filter by document type and process
cases.preconditions: documents tagged with document types and process areas
steps: Filters → Document type → Procedure.
Add Filters → Process area → a process.
cases.expected: the filters combine (AND); each pill removes independently; a library that lacks one of the columns is skipped quietly, never "Something refused"

cases.title: Filter by a person and by "has links"
cases.preconditions: documents with different owners; some with linked documents
steps: Filters → Owner → type a name and pick it.
Filters → Linked documents → "Has links".
cases.expected: only that owner's documents remain; the links filter then keeps the ones carrying links; the pills read "Owner: X" and "Has links"

cases.title: Filter by modified date
cases.preconditions: documents modified at different times
steps: Filters → Modified → last 30 days.
Custom range: pick a from date and a to date → Apply range.
Save the view; reopen it.
cases.expected: the list narrows to the window; the pill names it ("Modified: 1 Oct 2026 – 15 Oct 2026" for the range); either end of the range may be left open; a preset clears the range and the range clears the preset; the range is kept on a saved view; clearing restores the list

cases.title: Choose and order columns
cases.preconditions: a library with several available columns
steps: Kebab → Choose columns.
Untick one column, tick Version and Flags, drag Document below Modified, Apply.
Reload the page.
cases.expected: the register shows exactly the ticked columns in the dragged order, Document where it was placed with Library beside it; Version reads "v3.0" (a minor version muted); the choice survives a reload

cases.title: Sort by a column
cases.preconditions: any library
steps: Click the Modified header; click again.
Click the Document header.
cases.expected: the list sorts ascending then descending with the arrow in the header; name and Modified sort across the whole library, the other columns within the loaded rows

cases.title: Save, rename and tick a personal view
cases.preconditions: any library
steps: Set a search, a filter and a column set.
Views → Save view… → name it.
Change a filter; read the Views menu; Views → Rename… the view; pick it again.
cases.expected: the saved view appears in the menu with ✓ when active; after a change the title reads "View · name · edited"; Rename keeps the view; picking it restores search, filters and columns; the name box in the menu is wide enough to read

cases.title: Site views for everyone
cases.preconditions: signed in as a document controller
steps: Build a view with an organisation filter and a library; Views → "Save for the site".
Open the new site view from the Views menu straight away.
Sign in as a reader; open Views.
As the controller: Update site view, "✎ Rename", "× Delete".
cases.expected: opening the view paints the register with its filters (never a blank register — a view that cannot be applied falls back to the plain register with a line saying why); the title reads "View · name" only while the register still matches the view — clear a filter or click a folder and the title returns to the scope with the crumb "from the view “name” · edited" (Update and Close stay in the Views menu); the site view is listed under "Site views" for the reader, who can pick but not change it; Rename and Delete are labelled on the row, Delete asks first, and the controller's update, rename and delete take effect for everyone

cases.title: Favourites and Back to libraries
cases.preconditions: any library
steps: Star two documents (★ in the row).
Open ★ Favourites.
Click "← Back to libraries" at the far right.
cases.expected: Favourites lists the starred documents across libraries; Back returns to the tiles; the star is remembered per person

cases.title: The register on a phone
cases.preconditions: the app open on a phone (or a window under 600 px wide)
steps: Open Documents → a library.
Search; apply a status filter; open a document.
cases.expected: one stacked cell per document (name, status, owner, modified); search and filters work; the document opens in the viewer; no sideways scroll

cases.title: Open a document in the viewer
cases.preconditions: an approved PDF and a Word document
steps: Open the PDF from the register.
Close it; open the Word document.
cases.expected: the PDF renders in the viewer; the Word document shows its preview; the register's scroll position is restored on close; Esc closes

cases.title: The details pane
cases.preconditions: a document with owner, approvers, organisation, document id and a review date
steps: Open the document → Details.
Read the identity line, the chips and the Properties grid.
cases.expected: the id chip, status chip and the section headings match the library's column sections; dates read in the app's format; owner & approver collapse to one row when they are the same person; the review date's hint reads "in 9 months · every 12 months from the effective date (set by Importance: High)"; Organisation and Process area show the whole path ("Bell Bay › Casting"), the leaf alone only while the term walk loads or when two terms share the name

cases.title: Versions
cases.preconditions: a document with several versions; signed in as its OWNER (the Owner column names you) or as a document controller — anyone else sees no open links by design
steps: Open the document → Details → Versions.
Click a version's open link.
Sign in as a reader who is neither owner nor controller; open the same list.
cases.expected: every version with its label, author, date and comment; open links on versions for the owner or a controller only; the reader sees the list without the links and the line "Open links on versions show for the document's owner and document controllers"

cases.title: A Restricted View reader
cases.preconditions: a library where the test reader has Restricted View (no download)
steps: Open an approved PDF as that reader.
Look for Download, Open in new tab and the version list.
cases.expected: SharePoint's own viewer shows the document; no download or new-tab road; the current version line stands in for a history that would be refused; nothing errors

cases.title: Copy link, Download, Share with QR, Open in new tab
cases.preconditions: any PDF document
steps: Open the document → Copy link; paste it in a new browser tab.
Download (in the header, beside Open in new tab): read the saved file's name.
Share… → read the permalink and the QR code.
⋯ → Open in new tab ↗.
cases.expected: the pasted link opens LeanBoard on that document; Download saves the file under the document's own name (the viewer frame's own save icon cannot name it — it offers "pdf"); the QR encodes the same link; the new tab opens the file in SharePoint, and its tooltip says to print from there

cases.title: A permalink opens the document, a view link opens the view
cases.preconditions: a document permalink and a Documents view link (Views → Share view)
steps: Open the document permalink in a fresh browser tab.
Open the view link in a fresh browser tab.
cases.expected: the permalink lands on the document with the viewer open; the view link lands on the register with the view's library, filters and "Show only approved" state applied, not the default library

cases.title: Linked documents and "Show these in the register"
cases.preconditions: a document with three linked documents in its links column
steps: Open the document → Details → Linked documents.
Click one link; from there click one of ITS links; click "‹ Back to …" twice.
Back on the first document, click "Show these in the register".
cases.expected: the links are grouped by relationship; a click switches the viewer to the linked document and its header gains "‹ Back to <the first document>", which walks the trail back one step at a time; Esc still closes; opening a document from the register starts a fresh trail; "Show these" scopes the register to exactly those documents with the chip "Linked to: X", every other filter cleared; the chip's × restores the register

cases.title: Management of change chips
cases.preconditions: a document whose management-of-change column holds a record with a number and a link
steps: Read the register's MoC column.
Open the document → Details → the MoC row; click the chip.
cases.expected: the number reads as a chip in both places; the chip opens the link in a new tab; the tooltip carries the title and date

cases.title: Add a document to a working library
cases.preconditions: a working library the author may contribute to; a file to upload
steps: Open the working library → Add document → By upload → choose the file from your device (the upload folder stays as the second road where one is configured).
Leave a required field (the ones tagged "Required") empty; click Add.
Fill it; Add.
(Controller) Make a library column required that is not in the site dictionary; open Add document again.
(Controller) Make a dictionary column required through the library's CONTENT TYPE (not the column itself); open Add document again.
cases.expected: the device file goes straight into the library byte-exact (a name already in the library is refused before the upload); Approval status is not a form field — the document lands as a Draft, the lifecycle moves it from there; every required column carries a red "Required" tag on its label; a click on Add with one empty scrolls to the first, outlines each missing row and says "Required before Add: Owner, Importance" under the button, and the line clears as they are filled; the document then lands in the library with its properties and opens in the viewer, with the status line saying it was added as a draft, shows when "Show only approved" is unticked, and is submitted for review from its ⋯ menu; in step 4 the form names the library-required column it cannot collect and refuses before creating anything (no checked-out orphan); in step 5 the content-type-required column is tagged and validated like any other

cases.title: Add refuses a duplicate name and a duplicate document id
cases.preconditions: an existing document name and document id in the library; a second standards library carrying a document id
steps: Add document with the same file name.
Add document with a different name but the same document id.
Add document to the second library with a document id used in the first.
cases.expected: all three are refused before anything is written, each with a plain reason naming the clash ("A document named “X” already exists in this library — last modified by … on …" / "Document ID “X” is already used by “name” in <library>"); the check spans every standards library

cases.title: Edit properties
cases.preconditions: a draft standard you own
steps: Open the document → ⋯ → Edit properties…
Change a text field, a date, a taxonomy field and a person field; read the line under Importance.
Clear a required field; click Save; refill it; Save.
Edit again; change the document id to one another document carries; Save.
cases.expected: Approval status is not in the form (Submit / Approve / Retire move it); the dialog's footer stays pinned while the body scrolls; each editor fits its column type; under Importance a line reads "Sets the review cadence — High: every 12 months. Next review 17 Aug 2027, counted from the effective date 17 Aug 2026." and updates as Importance changes, with a read-only "Next review date · Derived" row beneath it; Save with a required field empty scrolls to it and names it under the buttons; Save then writes the values and the details pane shows them without reopening; the duplicate document id is refused with the clashing document named, and the unchanged id is never re-checked

cases.title: Cascading organisation and process pickers
cases.preconditions: the Organisation and Process area columns mapped
steps: Edit properties → Organisation: pick a company, then a site, then a department.
Process area: pick a type, then an area, then a process.
cases.expected: each level offers only the children of the level above; the saved value is the deepest pick; the register and filters read it back

cases.title: Management of change records
cases.preconditions: the management-of-change role mapped to a note column
steps: Edit properties → the Management of change rows: add a record with a number, a link typed without https, and what changed.
Add a second record; remove the first; Save.
cases.expected: each record is two lines (number and link, then what changed) and not cramped; a scheme-less link is accepted; the register cell shows the records as chips and the details pane shows one row per record — the number linking out, what changed, and the date

cases.title: Linked documents editor
cases.preconditions: the linked-documents column mapped; another document to link to
steps: Edit properties → Linked documents → Add link… search for a document, pick a relationship; add a second link.
Remove a link; Save.
cases.expected: the picker finds documents across the exposed libraries; two links save; the relationship is stored; the viewer's Linked documents section and the "n links" register cell follow. On a library whose Linked documents column is still a single line of text, the editor warns above the links and Save with two links is refused before anything is written, naming the column and the fix (multiple lines of text); Settings → Documents → Document columns carries the same warning on that column

cases.title: Check out, check in, discard
cases.preconditions: a draft standard you own, not checked out
steps: Open it → Check out.
Read the register row and the Document tasks panel.
Check in… with a comment (the Comment label is tagged Required, with the line "A comment is required — it is the version's audit entry"); then check out again and Discard check-out.
cases.expected: the row shows the lock and your name; "Checked out to you" lists it in Document tasks; Check in writes a minor version with the comment (the library must keep major AND minor versions — Settings → Documents warns on a library that keeps majors only); Discard releases it without a version; after an approval the published major's card carries the step's comment, or "published from v1.1 “…”" when the forms engine had to publish it

cases.title: Replace content
cases.preconditions: a draft standard you own; a new file
steps: Open it → ⋯ → Replace content…; choose a file of the same type from your device; Replace content.
Check in… with a comment.
cases.expected: the file goes over the document IN PLACE (the connector's Update file, bytes declared binary): the record keeps its id, every property, its links, favourites, flags and its history, and the new content sits on top as a version; a file of another type is refused before anything is sent; the dialog checks the landed size and the record identity and refuses to close on a mismatch; the document stays checked out to you; the check-in writes a minor version with the comment; the viewer reopens on the new content; a file over 100 MB (the connector's ceiling) is refused with "Replace it in SharePoint ↗" named, which stays as the second road

cases.title: Submit for review sends the reviewers' card at once
cases.preconditions: a draft standard you own with two reviewers named and a reviewer who can check Teams
steps: Open it → Submit for review.
Read the done line.
As a reviewer, check Teams.
cases.expected: the status becomes the mapped "in review" value; the done line names the status and ends "Reviewers notified ✓" without the notify panel asking first; each reviewer has a card with the document link

cases.title: Check in and submit for review as one flow
cases.preconditions: a draft standard you own (status Draft — on a document in review or later the one-flow button is rightly absent and the dialog says why), checked out to you
steps: Open it → Check in…
Click "Check in & submit for review".
cases.expected: one dialog does both; the version lands and the status moves to in review; the reviewers' card goes

cases.title: Review complete
cases.preconditions: a standard in review that names you as a reviewer
steps: Open it → Review complete.
Read the versions.
cases.expected: a minor version with the comment "Review complete by <you>"; the owner gets a Teams card; the action disappears for you once recorded

cases.title: Submit for approval warns while reviewers are outstanding
cases.preconditions: a standard in review with one reviewer done and one not
steps: Open it → Submit for approval.
Cancel at the warning; then run it again and confirm.
cases.expected: the warning names the reviewer who has not marked review complete; Cancel leaves the document untouched; Confirm proceeds to awaiting approval and the approvers' card goes

cases.title: Approve and publish
cases.preconditions: a standard awaiting approval that names you as approver; a cadence mapped to its importance
steps: Open it → Approve.
Read the status, the version, the effective date and the next review date.
cases.expected: a major version is published and approved; the effective date is today; the next review date is the effective date plus the cadence for its importance; the owner and reviewers get the courtesy card

cases.title: Owner approval and an owner outside the group
cases.preconditions: a standard awaiting owner approval whose owner is NOT in the owners & approvers group
steps: As that owner, open it.
Read the decision card.
cases.expected: "Awaiting your approval" with the reason the owner cannot approve and no Approve button; the controllers see the same document in health with "Add X to the group"

cases.title: Mark reviewed
cases.preconditions: an approved standard you own with a review date within 30 days
steps: Document tasks → Review due → open it → Mark reviewed.
Read the dates and the version comment.
cases.expected: the effective date refreshes, the next review date moves by the cadence, a minor version "Periodic review — no changes" is written; the task leaves the list

cases.title: Cancel a revision
cases.preconditions: an approved standard with a draft revision in progress (a minor version after the major), NOT checked out
steps: Open it → ⋯ → Cancel revision…
Confirm.
Repeat on a revision checked out to you; then on one checked out to someone else.
cases.expected: the last approved major's content and status come back as a NEW major (v3.0 restored lands as v4.0 with the comment "Revision cancelled — restored v3.0"), published where content approval is on; the draft versions stay in history; your own check-out is discarded first; another person's check-out refuses with their name

cases.title: Supersede and obsolete
cases.preconditions: two approved standards
steps: On one: ⋯ → Supersede…; search and pick the other as "Superseded by" (required); confirm.
On another approved standard: ⋯ → Make obsolete…
cases.expected: the superseded document carries the mapped status, a "Superseded by" link to its successor in its Linked documents and the comment "Superseded by “<name>”"; the successor's pane lists it under "Supersedes" (derived); the obsolete one carries its status; both leave the approved-only register and show when "Show only approved" is unticked

cases.title: The notify panel: Teams and email, people chips
cases.preconditions: a lifecycle step whose panel asks before sending (Submit for approval)
steps: Run the step; in the panel remove one recipient chip, add a note, choose Teams.
Run another step and choose Email.
cases.expected: the panel says "Nothing has been sent yet" above the chips; the chips show who hears and why; the removed person gets nothing; "Add a person…" finds someone in the directory and adds a chip; the note rides the card; "Send on Teams" / "Send by email" — the email arrives with the link; a refused send is reported with its reason, never silently

cases.title: Ask to work on a document
cases.preconditions: a working-library document the reader cannot edit
steps: Open it → Ask to work on this…; give a reason; Send.
Read Document tasks → Your access requests.
cases.expected: the request is recorded with the reason; the owner gets a Teams card; the reader sees it listed as pending

cases.title: Grant and decline
cases.preconditions: a pending request on a document you own
steps: Document tasks → Edit-access requests: read the request before deciding.
Approve.
On a second request: Decline with a reason.
cases.expected: each request is a card — the document name in full, who asked and when, the library, and the whole reason — with Open document, Approve… and Decline… beneath; the panel is wider while requests are listed; nothing is read for the first time inside the Approve dialog; Approve adds the person to the revision editors and the requester's card says so; Decline carries the reason; both leave the queue; the requester's "Your access requests" shows the outcome

cases.title: Revoke a grant
cases.preconditions: a grant you made earlier
steps: Document tasks → Edit access you granted → Revoke.
cases.expected: the person leaves the revision editors; the row leaves the list; the badge never counted this group

cases.title: The badge equals the panel
cases.preconditions: a mix of items awaiting you (approval, review, checked out, review due, a request)
steps: Read the Documents tab label and the "Document tasks · n" button.
Open the panel; count the rows across the groups.
cases.expected: the hub tab, the button and the panel agree on one number; the groups appear in order: requests, awaiting approval, awaiting review, checked out, review due, flagged, your requests, grants you made

cases.title: Open a task and show them all in the register
cases.preconditions: at least two task rows
steps: Click a task row.
Reopen the panel → "Show all n in register".
cases.expected: the row opens the document with its details pane and the action ready; "Show all" scopes the register with the chip "Document tasks · n", filters set aside; the chip's × restores the register

cases.title: Ingestion tasks from the register
cases.preconditions: an open ingestion task
steps: Read the "Ingestion tasks" button beside Document tasks.
Open it; open a task.
cases.expected: the button counts the open tasks you prepare or oversee; the panel lists them; a click opens the task sheet

cases.title: Suggest a tag from the properties
cases.preconditions: the Tags column mapped to a term set
steps: Open a document → Details → Properties → under Tags, "Suggest a tag…".
Type a new tag and why; Send proposal.
cases.expected: the link sits with the Tags property (a document with no tags still gets a Tags row holding it); the proposal is recorded and the status line says a controller decides; a duplicate label is refused

cases.title: The controllers' tag queue
cases.preconditions: a pending proposal raised on a DRAFT document
steps: Register kebab → "Tag proposals (n)…".
Approve the proposal.
cases.expected: the menu item counts the pending proposals; Approve mints the term, puts the tag on the draft document, and the proposer gets a Teams card saying so

cases.title: A tag on an approved document waits for its revision
cases.preconditions: a pending proposal raised on an APPROVED document
steps: Tag proposals → Approve it.
Read the queue; click "Tag now".
Start a revision on the document (check out), then "Tag now" again.
cases.expected: the term is minted but the document is not written; the proposal moves to "To tag at next revision" and the proposer's card says the tag goes on at the next revision; "Tag now" while approved says it is still approved; once in revision the tag lands and the proposal clears

cases.title: Decline a proposal
cases.preconditions: a pending proposal from another person
steps: Tag proposals → Decline… → give a reason.
cases.expected: the reason is required; the proposer's Teams card carries it; the proposal leaves the queue and stays on record as declined

cases.title: Tags in Settings
cases.preconditions: a pending proposal; tags in use
steps: Settings → Documents → Tags: read "Tags in use"; rename one; approve a pending proposal.
cases.expected: the rename keeps the term's id so tagged documents follow; approval behaves exactly as the controllers' queue (a tag on an approved document waits)

cases.title: Flag a document for review
cases.preconditions: a document owned by someone else; a screenshot on the clipboard
steps: Open it → under the buttons, "⚑ Flag for review…".
Pick a level, write a comment, paste the screenshot; Flag it.
cases.expected: the dialog names who will hear (the owner by name); a comment is required; the flag is written and the owner gets a Teams card quoting the comment with an "Open in LeanBoard" link; the owners are read fresh even when the register row never fetched them; flagging a document you own yourself raises the flag and says it sits in your Document tasks under Flags, with no Teams error (Teams cannot chat with yourself); a card to two or more people carries a topic with the quotes stripped

cases.title: A flag with no owner goes to the controllers
cases.preconditions: a document with no owner named
steps: Flag it.
cases.expected: the dialog says no owner is named and lists the controllers by name; the controllers get the card

cases.title: The flag chip and the flags list
cases.preconditions: a document you own carrying an open flag
steps: Open it → read the "⚑ level" chip under the buttons; click it.
In the list: read the screenshot; "Close flag…" with a note.
cases.expected: the chip names the level (or "n open flags"); the list shows level, flagger, when, comment and the screenshot full-size on click; closing asks for a note and the chip disappears; the closed flag stays listed for the record

cases.title: Flags in the register
cases.preconditions: open flags on several documents
steps: Choose columns → tick Flags.
Kebab → "Show flagged documents".
cases.expected: the Flags column reads "⚑ level" or "⚑ n open flags"; the scope lists only the flagged documents with the chip "Flagged for review · n"; the chip's × restores the register

cases.title: Flags in Document tasks and in health
cases.preconditions: an open flag on a document you own; another on a document you do not own
steps: Document tasks → "Flagged for review".
As a controller: the same group; and Document control health.
cases.expected: an owner sees the flags on their own documents only; a controller sees every open flag; the row shows level, flagger and the start of the comment and opens the document; health lists the flagged documents under "Flagged for review"

cases.title: The controllers' flags queue
cases.preconditions: open flags on the site
steps: Register kebab → "Document flags (n)…".
Open document; Close flag… with a note.
Settings → Documents → "Document flags…".
cases.expected: the queue lists every open flag with its screenshot; Open document opens the overlay; Close asks for a note and records who closed it; the Settings button opens the same queue

cases.title: Review levels are an app-managed list
cases.preconditions: Settings → Documents open
steps: Review levels: read the defaults marked "default"; add a level; Save.
Flag a document and read the level list.
cases.expected: adding a level replaces the defaults with your list (× on each); the flag dialog offers your list; an emptied list falls back to the defaults

cases.title: Mark reviewed offers to close the flags
cases.preconditions: an approved standard you own with two open flags and a review date within 30 days
steps: Mark reviewed.
At the prompt, Close flags.
cases.expected: after the review the prompt names each flag; confirming closes them with "Closed at Mark reviewed"; the chip clears and the tasks badge drops

cases.title: Create an ingestion task
cases.preconditions: the ingestion library exposed; a destination standards library
steps: Register kebab → New ingestion task…: name, destination, read the Site select (your own site preselected; "Any site" available), assignees, defaults — set the Status default to Approved; Create.
Open the task sheet; Open folder ↗.
cases.expected: Task defaults offers the Status column under its heading (it is set by hand in ingestion only — the documents arrive with their history); with a site chosen the Organisation unit default cascades from that site's term and the Process area default from the site's own tree, nothing beyond them; a sub-folder of the ingestion library is created and linked; the assignees get a Teams card; the sheet's meta line reads "→ library · <site> only · …" and shows the assignees and status chip

cases.title: Fill the grid
cases.preconditions: an open task you are assigned to with three files in its folder, two of them inside a sub-folder "Policies/2024"
steps: Refresh; read the ✱ required columns and the ⚠ marks; read the Document column.
Edit cells, including a Status cell from Draft to Approved; Fill blanks from defaults; Set for selected… on two rows, once with the Status column; Save.
Tick the checkbox on the "Policies › 2024" group row; Set for selected…; untick it.
cases.expected: the two nested files are listed with a muted "Policies › 2024" line under the name (read-only, the tooltip says the file lands flat) and sit under a group row "Policies › 2024 · 2 files · Open ↗" after the "Task folder" group; the group's checkbox selects exactly its files for Set for selected… and clears them again; sorting by another column drops the group rows and keeps the path lines; the Status cell and Set for selected… both offer the status editor (never "no editable columns configured"); on a task constrained to a site the Organisation unit and Process area cells and Set for selected… cascade from that site's branch only (the site itself is a valid pick), while an "Any site" task offers the whole sets; the header and every row share one set of column widths (no drift between rows); required cells drive the ✓/⚠ mark and its tooltip — a Management of change column is required only when SharePoint marks it so; the MoC cell shows its records as "MOC-12, MOC-14" and opens the records editor, never raw JSON; dirty cells and rows are marked until Save; emptying a text, choice or date cell that held a value, or Clear in a term / people popover, marks the cell dirty reading "—" and Save clears the value in SharePoint (a blank over a blank is nothing; the name never clears); Save writes the values to the ingestion items and the marks turn ✓; the Run button is greyed until every file is ready and saved

cases.title: Edit a task without losing its people
cases.preconditions: an open task with assignees
steps: Edit task… → change the name; Save.
Reopen the task.
cases.expected: the name changes and the assignees, defaults and log are intact; a stale copy is never saved over a newer one

cases.title: Status on landing
cases.preconditions: the status column in the grid; one file marked Approved, one Superseded, one Draft
steps: Run ingestion for the three.
Open each in the destination.
cases.expected: Approved and Superseded land as published majors with that status; Draft lands as a minor with the draft status; each file's version comment names the ingestion

cases.title: Flag a file during ingestion
cases.preconditions: an open task with a file
steps: In the "Flag for review" column (after the name column), "⚑ Flag…"; pick a level and comment.
Run the ingestion for that file; open it in the destination.
cases.expected: the pill shows in the column with the flagger and comment in its tooltip; the controllers get the card; after landing the flag is on the destination document with "raised in ingestion"

cases.title: Refusals are honest
cases.preconditions: a file whose name already exists in the destination; a file whose document id is already used; on a task constrained to a site, a file whose Organisation unit was set to another site's department in SharePoint's grid view; two files with the same name in different sub-folders of the task
steps: Read the two same-named files' ⚠ marks and the Run button; rename one with Name on ingestion and Save.
Run ingestion including the other three.
cases.expected: before the rename both same-named files read ⚠ "Missing: a unique name — another file in this task has the same name…", the status line counts "2 share a name" and Run is greyed; after the rename both are ✓; in the run each of the three is refused with the reason in its ⚠ tooltip and the run log — the third reads "Organisation unit "X" is outside this task's site (Y)"; the other files land flat in the destination (no sub-folder is created there); nothing half-moves

cases.title: Message assignees and end the task
cases.preconditions: an open task with at least one assignee who is not you, whose files have all moved; a second open task with files left in two sub-folders
steps: Message assignees… → read the recipients, type a note, Send.
End task… (the header button; the ✕ only closes the window and says so in its tooltip)
cases.expected: a dialog lists every assignee (you marked as not messaged — Teams refuses a chat with yourself) with a note box; Send shows the outcome in the dialog ("Teams message sent to …" or the refusal) and each other assignee gets the card with your note quoted under it; with you as the only assignee the dialog says so and Send is disabled; End task… confirms with the count of files not yet ingested, then the task closes with its log, leaves the open lists and the badge, and reopens from Settings if needed; on the second task End task… counts the FILES "(in 2 sub-folders)", not the folders, and Cancel task… in the task editor counts the same way

cases.title: Export the grid as a spreadsheet
cases.preconditions: an open task you are assigned to with files in its folder, some details saved; the owners & approvers group linked
steps: Edit a cell without saving; Export sheet.
Save (or Discard); Export sheet; open the workbook in Excel.
cases.expected: with unsaved changes the export is refused with "Save or discard your changes first"; otherwise a workbook `ingestion-<task>-<date>.xlsx` downloads; its Files sheet has one row per file, in folder-then-name order, with a LOCKED Folder column first ("Plans › 2024", blank at the root — Excel refuses to type in it, the guidance says it is for reference), then Name on ingestion and every grid column (the MoC column left out); every other cell edits freely and rows can be added, deleted, sorted and filtered (the sheet is protected only on the id and Folder columns), term cells as full paths ("Pechey › Bell Bay › Casting"), people as "Name <email>", dates as real Excel dates shown yyyy-mm-dd, required columns marked ✱; under the header a muted guidance row says how to fill each column ("Required. One term as its full path — use the dropdown…", "A date — type yyyy-mm-dd or pick a date…"); the header, guidance and key rows are frozen; typing "Nov 3" into a date cell is refused by Excel, a typed date shows as yyyy-mm-dd; column A and row 2 are hidden keys; the Values sheet lists every term path, choice and the owners & approvers pool per column — on a task constrained to a site, the Organisation unit and Process area paths are that site's branch only, starting at the site; a single-value term, choice or owner cell offers an Excel dropdown of those values and refuses a typed value outside them

cases.title: Upload an edited spreadsheet
cases.preconditions: the workbook from DOC-087
steps: In Excel: change a status from the dropdown, pick an owner, type a term's leaf label ("Casting") in another file's organisation cell by pasting over the validation, empty a title cell, rename a file in Name on ingestion, try to type into a Folder cell (refused — then unprotect the sheet from the Review tab and change one), type "Nov 3" in a date cell, and delete a file's row; save.
Upload sheet… → drop or choose the workbook; read the report; Apply to grid; Save changes.
cases.expected: the report says how many cells on how many files change and lists each problem with its Excel row, file, column, value and reason — the leaf label says to use the full path, "Nov 3" says yyyy-mm-dd — a Folder cell changed after unprotecting is ignored without a problem line, and the deleted row's file is simply untouched; Apply marks the changed cells dirty in the grid (the emptied title reads "—"), leaves the problem cells as they were, and the status line counts the problems; Save writes the changes, renames the file, and clears the title in SharePoint; uploading the untouched export reports "0 cells on 0 files to change" with Apply greyed; a workbook that is not this task's export is refused with a message, nothing applied

cases.title: A nested drop lists and lands flat
cases.preconditions: an open task; in SharePoint, a folder tree dropped into its folder — files at the root, in "Policies", in "Policies/2024" and in "Archive/2019"; one file renamed in the grid
steps: Refresh the task; read the status line and the grid.
Rename a nested file with Name on ingestion; Save; check the file in SharePoint.
Set every required detail (use the group checkboxes); Run.
End task.
cases.expected: every file at every depth is listed — the status line reads "n files in 3 sub-folders · …"; the grid groups them under Task folder, Archive › 2019, Policies, Policies › 2024 with the path under each nested name; the renamed file keeps its place in its sub-folder (it does not move to the task root); the run copies every file into the destination library's ROOT with no sub-folder created, the sources are recycled and the emptied sub-folders stay; End task counts 0 files and removes the folder with its empty sub-folders

journeys.title: Journey 10 — Health and the term store

cases.title: The owners & approvers group from the register
cases.journey: Journey 10 — Health and the term store
cases.preconditions: the owners & approvers group linked (Settings → Access control); you own it in Entra (a super admin added you to Document controllers); someone in the directory who is not in the group
steps: Register kebab → Owners & approvers group…; read the ownership line and the members.
Search the directory for the person; ＋ Add.
Open Edit properties on a standard and search the Owner picker for them.
Back in the dialog, Remove them; confirm.
cases.expected: the dialog says you own the group and lists its members with mail; the add lands with a tick and the person is at once offered by the owner and approver pickers (no reload); Remove asks first and names what they lose; a controller who does NOT own the group sees the members only, with a line saying who can make them an owner

cases.title: Document control health
cases.journey: Journey 10 — Health and the term store
cases.preconditions: documents with a missing owner, a missing status, an overdue review, no tags, a review date the app cannot read
steps: Register kebab → Document control health…
Expand each finding; click a document.
cases.expected: each finding lists its documents with a reason and the fix; a review date the feed renders in the site's locale ("17/08/2027" on an Australian site) is read as a date, so "Review date unreadable" fires only for a value that is not a date at all; the CSV's "Review source" column says whether each date came from the feed or was read from the text; a document opens from the report; the summary counts clean documents

cases.title: People findings: leavers, outside the group, replace a person
cases.journey: Journey 10 — Health and the term store
cases.preconditions: a document naming a person who left the directory; an owner outside the owners & approvers group
steps: Health → the people findings: "Add X to the group" on the outsider; "Replace X…" on the leaver with a successor.
Teams digest to controllers; Export CSV.
cases.expected: Add puts the person in the group and the finding clears on refresh; Replace rewrites the role on every listed document; the digest card reaches the controllers; the CSV carries a People column; a directory lookup that failed is reported as "Not checked", never as absent

cases.title: Organisation term sync and the drift report
cases.journey: Journey 10 — Health and the term store
cases.preconditions: Settings → Organisation with sites under companies; the Organisation term set bound
steps: Settings → Documents → Term store → Load drift report.
Read matched / to create / orphans; Apply.
Change a department name in Settings → Organisation; Save; reload the drift report.
cases.expected: the walk reads the whole set (never a cut-short walk); companies are top-level terms when the set starts at company level; ampersand and dash variants match; the rename is written through to the term; orphans offer Leave / Retire / "This is…"

cases.title: Process area sync
cases.journey: Journey 10 — Health and the term store
cases.preconditions: at least one site with its own process tree (Settings → Processes) and a central type that still carries retired local names; the Process area set bound
steps: Settings → Documents → Term store → Load process drift report → Apply.
Archive a process node in a site's tree; reload the report.
cases.expected: every SITE node is a term in order under a root term named after the site (the central types do not sync); the old type-rooted terms are listed as orphans and left alone; the synonyms the retired local names once pushed are removed from the central nodes' terms and the nodes' local names clear; an archived node's term is retired, never deleted

cases.title: Compare documents across sites by process
cases.journey: Journey 10 — Health and the term store
cases.preconditions: two sites with process trees whose nodes link to the same central process; a document on each tagged with that site's process term; a Process area column mapped
steps: Register → Filters → the Process area column → "Compare across sites" → pick the central type and process.
cases.expected: the filter chip names the central process; the register shows the documents of BOTH sites tagged with their own linked process terms (and anything beneath them); clearing the chip shows everything again

cases.title: Connection and libraries
cases.preconditions: the SharePoint site url known
steps: Settings → Documents → SharePoint connection: test it.
Libraries: discover; expose a library as Standard; set its title; Save.
cases.expected: the test reports the site and the groups it can read; a newly exposed library appears as a register tile with the site columns it carries ticked

cases.title: Document columns and roles
cases.preconditions: the site columns created in SharePoint
steps: Document columns: map each role; set a label; reorder by drag; Save.
Open a document's details.
cases.expected: every role maps to one column and the duplicate-role check refuses a second; labels and order are what the viewer and the add form show

cases.title: Lifecycle mapping and review cadence
cases.preconditions: the Status term set with one term per stage
steps: Lifecycle: map each stage to its term; Save.
Review cadence: set months per importance term; Save.
cases.expected: the lifecycle commands appear on documents according to their status; a document's next review date follows the cadence of its importance on approval and Mark reviewed

cases.title: Default filters, write access and the move road
cases.preconditions: Settings → Documents open
steps: Default filters: set a default organisation; Save; open the register as a reader.
Write access: run the probe. Move road: run the probe.
cases.expected: the reader's register opens on the default organisation; each probe reports what it tried and what SharePoint answered, in plain words

cases.title: Access control groups
cases.preconditions: the controllers and owners & approvers groups exist
steps: Settings → Documents → the groups: pick each; Save.
Sign in as a controller; as a plain owner.
cases.expected: the controller sees the controller-only kebab items (Tag proposals, Document flags, health, ingestion); the owner outside the group cannot approve; a group that cannot be read is reported, never assumed empty

cases.title: Documents health check from the kebab
cases.preconditions: Documents health checks enabled for the site (Settings → Health checks)
steps: Register kebab → "Health check…"; keep the site in the picker; run and submit.
cases.expected: the item shows for controllers only; the check is scoped to the site; the full behaviour is in the Health checks script

cases.title: Documentation & links card
cases.preconditions: an initiative board with a Documentation & links card and a working folder set
steps: On the card, expand a sub-folder; open a file.
Add a link; remove it.
cases.expected: sub-folders expand in place with carets; files open in SharePoint; links save on the board and the register's "n links" follows when the card is bound to a document

cases.title: Document cards on a board
cases.preconditions: a ritual board with a Document health card and a Standard documents card
steps: Open the board; read both cards.
Click a row on the health card.
cases.expected: the health card shows the same task rows as Document tasks for that scope; the documents card lists the configured documents; a click opens the document in the viewer

cases.title: The Documents panel resizes
cases.preconditions: the register open on a desktop
steps: Drag the panel's right edge narrower, then wider.
Reload.
cases.expected: the Folders pane follows the drag between its limits, labels wrap instead of clipping, and the width is remembered

journeys.title: Journey 13 — End to end, several people

cases.title: A reader's revision, from request to publication
cases.journey: Journey 13 — End to end, several people
cases.preconditions: an approved standard with an owner, a reviewer and an approver named; a reader not named on it; the Revision editors column mapped
steps: [Reader] Open the standard → "Request edit access…" with a reason.
[Owner] Document tasks → the request → Approve & grant; send the card.
[Reader] From the card's link: Start revision; Check out & edit; Check in with a comment.
[Reader] Submit for review; keep the reviewer; Send on Teams.
[Reviewer] From the card: open → Review complete with a comment.
[Reader] Submit for approval; Send on Teams.
[Approver] From the card: Approve with a comment.
[Everyone] Reopen the standard.
cases.expected: the request shows in the owner's Document tasks and nowhere else; the grant lands at once and the reader's card opens the document with Start revision live; the draft minor carries the reader's comment; the reviewer's task appears on submit and clears on Review complete; the approver's task appears and clears on Approve; the approved major carries "Approved by <approver> — <comment>" and the review date moves by the cadence; the reader's grant is released; readers see the new content only after the approval

cases.title: A revision sent back, fixed and approved
cases.journey: Journey 13 — End to end, several people
cases.preconditions: a draft revision in review; its owner, the reviewer and an approver on separate devices
steps: [Reviewer] Open → Request revision with a reason.
[Owner] Document tasks → the document → Check out & edit → Check in → Submit for review.
[Reviewer] Review complete.
[Owner] Submit for approval.
[Approver] Approve.
cases.expected: Request revision returns the status to Draft with the reason in the version comment and on the owner's card; the owner's Document tasks lists it under "Needs revision"; the second review and the approval run as in DOC-082; the version history shows every step with its comment

cases.title: A flag raised by a reader, acted on by the owner
cases.journey: Journey 13 — End to end, several people
cases.preconditions: an approved standard; a reader; its owner
steps: [Reader] Flag for review… with a level and a comment.
[Owner] From the Teams card: open → read the flag chip → Mark reviewed… and accept "close the open flags".
[Reader] Reopen the document.
cases.expected: the owner's card quotes the comment with an Open link; the flag shows on the register row and in the owner's Document tasks; Mark reviewed offers to close the open flags and the chip clears; the reader sees no open flag

cases.title: Supersede with a successor, seen by everyone
cases.journey: Journey 13 — End to end, several people
cases.preconditions: two approved standards (A the old, B the new); a controller; a reader
steps: [Controller] On A: ⋯ → Supersede…; pick B as "Superseded by"; confirm.
[Reader] Open A; follow its "Superseded by" link; read B's pane.
cases.expected: A carries the Superseded status and a "Superseded by" link to B; B's pane lists A under "Supersedes" (derived); A leaves the approved-only register and shows with "Show only approved" unticked; the reader reaches B from A's link and "‹ Back to A" returns

cases.title: Define standard criteria
cases.preconditions: Settings → Health checks open as a super admin
steps: Under Cadence health check → Standard criteria → ＋ Add standard criterion; title and description.
Add three questions, one of each form: Yes / no, All / some / no, Select from a list (give the list three choices with guidance and weights).
Change a Yes / no weight; tick "Allow not applicable" on one question; reorder criteria and questions with the ⠿ handle or ▲▼.
Save.
cases.expected: every edit buffers until Save; a criterion with no title, a list with fewer than two choices or a choice without a title, or a question with no answer worth anything refuses the save naming the problem; after Save the criteria reload as entered, marked "standard"; Yes / no defaults to 1 / 0 and All / some / no to 1 / 0.5 / 0

cases.title: Site criteria and the enable switch
cases.preconditions: a site admin at a site; standard criteria exist
steps: Settings → Health checks: read the standard criteria (no editing, no hiding).
Under the site's criteria → ＋ Add the site criterion with a question.
Tick "Enabled for <site>" on Cadence; Save.
cases.expected: the standard criteria are read-only for a site admin with no way to hide one; the site criterion saves marked with the site; the switch turns the type on for the site only

cases.title: Recent checks per site
cases.preconditions: checks exist at two sites
steps: Settings → Health checks: use the site picker at the top.
Read "Recent checks" under a type; Open one.
cases.expected: a super admin switches sites and sees each site's recent checks (date, scope, score, assessor); a site admin sees their own site only; Open shows the check read-only

cases.title: Meeting health check from the board
cases.preconditions: Cadence checks enabled for the site; a ritual you own or attend
steps: Open the ritual's board: a "Health check" button sits left of Live board.
Click it; answer every question; type What went well and Even better if.
Submit.
cases.expected: the popup shows the criteria as cards — statements under a Yes | No (or All | Some | No) column strip with one tick per row, list questions as rows of choice, guidance and a tick — the score live in the footer, "n questions to answer" under Submit until none remain; Submit records the check and the button reads "Health check · 3.4"; the button is absent when the type is off for the site

cases.title: Draft, Reset, Discard
cases.preconditions: a scope with no check today
steps: Start a check, answer some questions, Close.
Reopen: the answers are there (a draft); the button reads "Health check · draft".
Reset → confirm: every answer clears, the comments stay.
Discard draft → confirm.
cases.expected: a draft is kept and reopened as the day's check on that scope; Reset clears the ticks only; Discard removes it and the button reads "Health check" again

cases.title: N/A and the score
cases.preconditions: a criterion with an N/A-allowed question
steps: Answer every question but the N/A one; read the footer.
Mark it N/A.
Read each card's own score and the overall.
cases.expected: an unanswered question blocks Submit; N/A removes it from both numerator and denominator; each card shows its own 0–5 and the footer the weighted whole to one decimal with the five-segment bar

cases.title: One check per scope per day; edit for seven days
cases.preconditions: a check submitted today on a scope by another person
steps: Open the scope's Health check button as a different assessor.
Change an answer; Save changes.
On a check submitted more than seven days ago (or a void one), open it from the trend.
cases.expected: the button opens today's existing check, not a second one; a submitted check is editable by anyone who may run it, and the header names who edited it; a check older than seven days is read-only ("locked")

cases.title: Trend and past checks
cases.preconditions: a scope with three submitted checks
steps: Open the check: read the Trend strip.
Click an earlier chip; read it; "← Back to today's check".
cases.expected: the strip lists the last six submitted checks newest first with date and score; an earlier check opens read-only in the same dialog; Back returns to today's

cases.title: Actions from a check
cases.preconditions: a meeting check open
steps: ＋ Add action; fill it in; save.
Read the Actions row; open the board's Actions card.
cases.expected: the action lands on the board's channel and shows on the board's Actions card; the check lists it with its status; for a priorities or documents check the action lands on the assessor's own list instead

cases.title: Initiative health check
cases.preconditions: Initiative checks enabled; an initiative you hold a role on
steps: Open the initiative board: Health check left of Live board.
Run and submit.
Open the initiative's Details pane and the Improvement list.
cases.expected: the check runs against the Initiative criteria; the Details pane no longer has the old "Health check" button and the Improvement list no longer has a Health column

cases.title: Priorities health check per sub-pillar
cases.preconditions: Priorities checks enabled; an org you manage with sub-pillars
steps: Priorities → "Health check…" after ＋ Priority: a picker of the org's sub-pillars with their last score and date.
Pick one; run and submit.
Read the sub-pillar's column header; then ⋮ → Show → Health check scores and read it again.
Click the chip.
cases.expected: one sub-pillar at a time; the check is scoped to the sub-pillar at this organisation; the header shows NO chip until Health check scores is on (off by default, remembered per person); on, a small white "3.4" sits at the header's right edge on one line however narrow the column, its tooltip carrying the date and "of 5"; a check older than 90 days is a hollow outline chip; clicking the chip opens that sub-pillar's check (read-only for someone who cannot run one)

cases.title: Documents health check
cases.preconditions: Documents checks enabled; signed in as a document controller
steps: Documents → kebab → "Health check…".
In the org picker, keep your site or pick a department; run and submit.
cases.expected: the kebab item is there for controllers only; the picker opens on the person's site; the check is scoped to the chosen organisational level

cases.title: Void and restore
cases.preconditions: a submitted check
steps: Open it; Void… with a reason.
Read the trend; open the void check from "n void"; Restore.
cases.expected: a void check leaves the trend and the recent list and stays on record marked void with who and why; Restore puts it back; a submitted check is never deleted

cases.title: The trend's time axis
cases.preconditions: a monthly metric with two readings (this month and last); a weekly metric with readings over three months; a daily metric with a missed day
steps: Open the board; read the monthly card's chart.
Read the weekly card's chart.
Read the daily card's chart.
cases.expected: the monthly chart spans twelve months ending at the current month, each month ticked and named, the two readings sitting at their months at the right; the weekly chart shows its full three months (more than the 13-week floor) with thinned labels; the daily chart shows four weeks with the missed day as a gap in the line; plan, forecast and limit labels keep their place at the right edge

cases.title: Cadence across sites by process
cases.preconditions: two sites whose process trees link a node each to the same central process; a ritual on each site naming its site's node
steps: Hub → Cadence (or the Rituals directory) → scope "Organisation" with no site: read the Process filter — a type, then the central cascade; pick the central process.
Pick a site in the organisation cascade: read the Process filter again.
cases.expected: at company scope the central pick shows both rituals (each matches through its site node's link) and the pick is remembered with the scope; with a site chosen the Process filter cascades through that site's own tree and a leftover central pick is cleared; a site with no tree shows no Process filter

cases.title: Tiles fill their slot at a readable size
cases.preconditions: a ritual board with several live tiles (an agenda, an action board, a status tile); a laptop (about 1366 px) and, if available, a wall screen
steps: Open the board on the laptop with the details pane closed, then open the pane; read the tiles.
Set the board to three or four columns with the pane open; read the tiles.
Open a card from the board (the focused view) on the laptop and on the widest screen available.
cases.expected: tiles fill their slot with no empty band beside or below the card and the text stays readable (never thumbnails) — a wide slot shows a wide card, a tall slot a tall one; a tile shows no scrollbar; when the slots become too narrow (three or more columns with the pane open) the board flips to the one-per-row list rather than shrinking further; the focused card is centred and no wider than about 1600 px on a big monitor and full width on the laptop; the action rows inside a narrow tile read as two lines

cases.title: Tables fit their card
cases.preconditions: a capture card with five text columns and twenty rows; a capture rollup over two boards; a RACI with six roles and ten deliverables; a skills matrix with eight people
steps: Open each as a tile on a board, then focused; scroll the focused view down and, where it overflows, sideways.
cases.expected: a capture table never scrolls sideways in a tile or the focused view at laptop width — the columns share the width and long cells wrap; scrolling down keeps the column heads in view and scrolling sideways (a rollup with many fields) keeps the Source / charter column in view; the RACI keeps its role heads and deliverable labels in view the same way, the skills matrix its people heads and skill labels

cases.title: Diagrams keep fitting until you take over
cases.preconditions: a five-whys card with a five-step chain, a fault tree, a process map; a window you can resize
steps: Open each focused; resize the window narrower and wider; open the details pane and close it.
Pan the diagram a little, then resize again; press ⤢ Fit to view.
cases.expected: before you touch it, the diagram refits to every size change — a small five-whys chain grows past 1:1 to fill a wide window (up to 1.5×), a big one shrinks to fit; after a pan or a zoom the view stays where you put it through further resizes; Fit to view hands the fitting back; as a tile the diagram never enlarges past 1:1

cases.title: Content cards follow their host
cases.preconditions: a ritual board with an agenda, an action board set to Gantt, a status tile, a capture card with two rows and a links card with nine links in two groups; an initiative board with its charter; a laptop (about 1366 px) and the widest screen available
steps: On the laptop with the details pane open, read the board's tiles; then open each card focused.
Widen the card (close the pane, or the big screen); narrow it (the pane open, or a split).
Links: as a tile, count the links shown and read "+n more"; focused on the wide screen, read the layout.
cases.expected: the agenda tile clips without a scrollbar and, when narrow, puts who · minutes under each title in one row; the action board's kanban columns share the width with no sideways scrollbar, and a Gantt asked for in a card under about 760 px shows the list with "The Gantt opens when the card is wider"; the charter TILE shows the whole canvas scaled to fit (never cut at row five) and the focused charter's rows grow to fill a tall window; a two-row capture card's big text never wraps a word a line (it is capped by the column width); the status tile's state word and reason grow and shrink with the box and a long reason stops at three lines; the links tile shows exactly six LINKS (group headings do not count) and "+3 more"; on the wide screen the links lay out in columns; an embed card's commentary pane sits under the frame when the card is narrow

cases.title: Matrices and grids follow their host
cases.preconditions: a board with a risk matrix (six risks), a RACI (six roles, eight deliverables), a skills matrix (four people), a conditions card, an SQDPC card with all five letters and a heatmap with a list; a laptop and, if available, a phone
steps: Read each as a tile on the laptop with the details pane open, then focused; widen and narrow the card.
On the phone (or a pane under 480 px) read the risk matrix, the RACI and the heatmap.
cases.expected: the risk matrix's cells grow square with the card and the register drops under the matrix when the two do not fit side by side; in a narrow tile the register is hidden and the matrix fits without sideways scroll; the RACI's label column gives way before the cells, a read-only RACI has no Actions column, and under 480 px each deliverable's name sits on its own row above its cells with the roles as initials (hover for the name); the skills matrix's columns stop growing at 96 px and a tile hides its Actions row; the conditions card's label column narrows with the card (down to 90 px) with the legend aligned under it and the name text shrinking to fit; the SQDPC letters wrap into two or three rows in a narrow box with the tile size chosen for that wrap, and digits vanish under 18 px; the heatmap's list sits under the image on a narrow host and is hidden in a narrow tile

cases.title: Charts draw at the size they are shown
cases.preconditions: a KPI trend card with readings and a Pareto with twelve categories; a laptop, the widest screen available and, if possible, a phone
steps: Read both as tiles, then focused; widen and narrow the card.
cases.expected: the trend chart fills its box with no blank band above or below, and its tick and value text reads the same size (about 10–12 px) in a tile, on the laptop and on the big screen — never giant on a 27" monitor, never specks on a phone; the Pareto likewise, and when the card is narrow the tail of small categories folds into one greyed "Other (n)" bar that cannot be tapped while the vital few keep their names; widening the card unfolds them

cases.title: Show completed, edit from the Gantt, Gantt lanes follow the kanban columns
cases.preconditions: a board whose Action card has two or more completed actions and some open ones; a second Action card configured with custom kanban columns (grouped by issue, e.g. Safety · Quality · Delivery) with actions in at least two columns
steps: Open the first card. On the List view read the "Show completed" switch; switch to Kanban, then Gantt, reading it each time.
Switch it on, then off again; look at the Kanban's Done column while it is off.
Mark every action complete, then look at the card.
On the Gantt, click an action's name; change its description; save. Then drag a bar.
Open the second card on the Gantt.
cases.expected: step 1 the switch is present on all three views and OFF, with the hidden count in brackets, and completed actions appear on none of them; step 2 on, completed actions show on the list, in Done and as grey bars; off again, the Done column stays as a drop target reading "n completed hidden", and clicking that line switches completed on; step 3 the card reads "All n actions are complete" with the switch and the Add button, not the empty-card prompt; step 4 the action's dialog opens from its name and the saved change shows; the bar still drags its dates; step 5 the Gantt shows a lane per kanban column in the kanban's order with a count, each folding to one summary bar on click, and the list view inside the Gantt groups the same way

cases.title: Quick add on an initiative board links to that initiative
cases.preconditions: three initiatives with boards — one active you hold a role on, one COMPLETED, one confidential you hold no role on but whose board you can open
steps: Open each initiative's board (the overview) and press the top bar's ＋ Add action; read the "Linked to" chip; type an issue; Save. On the active one, press Save the instant the dialog opens, before the link has loaded.
Open each initiative's Action plan and the person's My day.
cases.expected: the chip names the initiative on all three — the completed and the confidential ones read "Initiative · <its title>" even though they are not in your search list — and every action, the fast-saved one included, appears on its initiative's Action plan and on the board's action card; none sits on My day as a personal action; the row's source reads leanhub and its key names the board

cases.title: Unlinking stays unlinked
cases.preconditions: an action raised from a card on an initiative board
steps: Open the card's ＋ Action → the action → press the chip's ✕ (Take it off) → Save.
Open the action from My day; reopen the initiative's Action plan.
cases.expected: the action leaves the card and the initiative's Action plan and shows on My day as "Personal — not linked"; it is NOT re-linked to the initiative behind the scenes (the row has no initiative id); linking it back from My day's search restores it to the initiative

cases.title: The driver tree's process filter, this site or across sites
cases.preconditions: two sites with value driver trees whose drivers name site process nodes linked to the same central process
steps: Value drivers (the hub tab) on the first site: Process → the mode select reads "This site" → pick an area; read the dimming.
Switch the mode to "Across sites" → pick the type and the central process; read the dimming; switch the Site select to the second site.
Settings → Value drivers: the same Process bar on the structure editor.
cases.expected: "This site" cascades through the site's own tree and dims the drivers outside the pick; "Across sites" dims the drivers whose process does not link to the central pick, and the pick HOLDS when the site changes (the second site's tree dims by the same central process); the structure editor's bar behaves the same; a site with no tree offers "Across sites" only, and no bar at all when the central hierarchy is empty

cases.title: Linking a priority from the new-initiative form
cases.preconditions: a site with priorities at the company, the site and one department; the Improvement tab scoped to that department
steps: Improvement → New initiative → pick a template; read the Organisation group's site, department and area.
Priorities & people → "＋ Link a priority"; read the list; type part of a company priority's statement; clear it; press "n more from above ›".
Change the department in the form to one with no priorities of its own; open the picker again.
cases.expected: step 1 the form opens on the tab's scope, department included; step 2 the picker opens with the search box focused and lists only the department's open priorities under its name, with one line "n more from above ›"; typing narrows both the department's and the parents' priorities case-blind and shows the parents' groups; the line expands the company and site groups in chain order; step 3 a department without its own priorities shows "No open priorities at <department>" and the parents' groups straight away; Edit details on an existing initiative uses the same picker

cases.title: The Objectives row lists metrics only
cases.preconditions: a wall with three or more priorities in view: one whose primary initiative has starred metrics with values, one whose primary initiative has none starred, one with no primary initiative
steps: Priorities tab in the matrix view; read the Objectives row under each column.
Switch to the present view and step to the same priorities.
cases.expected: the Objectives row shows "Name: objective" with plan / actual and a traffic light for each starred metric, and is BLANK under a priority with no starred metric or no primary initiative — no "No primary initiative" or "No metric value yet" line anywhere in the row; the present view shows the same lines and the same blanks

cases.title: The ⋮ menu: no period, a health-chip toggle
cases.preconditions: a wall with at least one sub-pillar that has a submitted health check
steps: Priorities tab → ⋮ in the toolbar: read the sections.
Change the year with the year pill in the header.
⋮ → Show → Health check scores; close and reopen the app.
cases.expected: the menu has Status · View · Roll-up rule · Show · Share and no Period section — the year pill (and the phone head's Period select) is the one period door; Health check scores is off by default and the headers carry no chip; on, the chips appear and the choice is remembered for this person across sessions

cases.title: A site admin adds a person from the directory
cases.preconditions: signed in as a site admin; someone in the directory who is not yet on the roster
steps: Settings → People; type the person's name in the search box; "Search directory & add".
On the hit, ＋ Add; read the placement row; pick a department and crew; "Add to roster".
Search the roster for them.
cases.expected: the note at the top says site admins add people from the directory into their site; the directory matches show; the placement row's Site is fixed to the admin's own site and Role to User (both greyed, with a tooltip saying why), department and crew offer the site's own; the person lands on the roster placed in that site; a super admin sees the full placement row with every site and role

cases.title: Members of the document control groups
cases.preconditions: the Document controllers and Owners & approvers groups linked under Settings → Access control, both owned by you in Entra; a person in the directory who is in neither
steps: Settings → Access control → Document controllers → Members…; read the note and the ownership line.
Search the directory for the person; ＋ Add. In Entra (or the Owners & approvers → Members… dialog) check the owners & approvers group.
Remove them from Document controllers; confirm. Check the owners & approvers group again.
Owners & approvers → Members…: add and remove someone.
Settings → Users: read the Document roles column; tick Controller on a person; untick Owner/approver on another.
cases.expected: the Users register's Document roles column shows a Controller and an Owner/approver box per person, ticked from the groups' live membership, writable only for a super admin who owns the group (the tooltip says why otherwise, and your own Controller box cannot be unticked); ticking Controller also ticks Owner/approver; unticking asks first and a refusal reverts the box with the reason under the row; Members… shows only on a linked group; the controllers dialog says an add also makes the person a member and owner of the owners & approvers group; after the add they are a controller AND a member and owner of the pool; after the remove they are no controller and no longer an owner of the pool but still its member; the pool dialog adds and removes members alone; removing the group's only owner is refused with a readable line; you cannot remove yourself

cases.title: A site's own process hierarchy
cases.preconditions: you are a site admin of a site with no process hierarchy yet; the central hierarchy has a type with areas and processes
steps: Settings → Processes: your site is the only chip; read the starter.
Clone the central type (or Start empty); add an area, a process beneath it and a sub-process; rename one; reorder two by drag; archive one.
Open a ritual's wizard, an initiative's header form and a value driver for your site.
cases.expected: the tab shows only your site, no Central hierarchy chip; cloning creates the tree in the site's own words with every node reading "↔ <central name>" greyed (a super admin sets links) and the status line counts the rituals, initiatives and value drivers re-pointed; edits write at once and the term-set push line reads under the tree; the pickers in the wizard, the initiative form and the value driver cascade through YOUR site's tree, never the central one

cases.title: Links to the central hierarchy
cases.preconditions: a site with its own tree; the central hierarchy with two types
steps: Settings → Processes → the site chip → "↔" on an area → pick a type and a central process → Link.
On a process beneath that area read its link; open it and press Inherit.
Central hierarchy chip → the type → read the "↔ n site nodes" count on the central node; rename it.
cases.expected: the area reads "↔ Type › Process"; the node beneath reads the same with "(inherited)"; Inherit on a node with its own link clears it back to the inherited one; the central node's count shows the explicit links; renaming a central node does not touch the term set (the central tree does not sync) and the site node's label in the Improvement tab's company-scope filter follows

cases.title: Initiatives compared across sites
cases.preconditions: two sites whose trees link a node each to the same central process; an initiative on each naming its site's node
steps: Improvement tab at company scope (no site) → Filters → "Process (across sites)" → the type, then the process.
Switch the scope to one site → Filters → Process.
cases.expected: at company scope both initiatives match the central pick and the filter count reads 1; at site scope the Process filter cascades through that site's own tree and matches only its initiative

cases.title: People on an old build are told, then gated
cases.preconditions: two devices (or a browser and the phone) open on the app; Settings → Branding → Version readable
steps: Settings → Branding → Version: read "This device", "Current build" and "Oldest build allowed". Press "Make this build current" if it is not.
Leave device B open. Push a new build (or on device A press "Make this build current" after a push). Wait up to five minutes on device B, or switch away from its tab and back.
On device B close LeanBoard and open it again.
On device A press "Require this build"; on a device still on the older build, open a card editor, make a change, wait.
Settings → Users: find the two people.
cases.expected: step 1 names the device's build (v0.x.y, "+n" past a tag) and who recorded the current one; step 2 device B shows an amber banner under the top bar naming both builds and asking to close and reopen, nothing is blocked; a device that OPENS on the old build (a cached player) sees the full-screen gate instead and cannot use the app; step 3 clears it and, on a clean build newer than the record, records itself as current; step 4 the old device shows the red banner while the editor holds unsaved work and the gate as soon as it is saved or closed; "Clear the minimum" lifts it; step 5 each person's row reads "Last opened on <build>"

cases.title: Import a site's team from the directory
cases.preconditions: a site with a site owner and at least one department owner set in Settings → Organisation; some of that site's people not yet on the roster; one of them placed on a different site
steps: Settings → Users → "Import a site's team…" → pick the site; read the "Start from" chip; add a second starting person by search; remove it again.
Walk the directory; watch the progress line.
In the list: read the counts; find a person under a department owner and read their proposed department; find the one on another site; tick "Show skipped and already here".
Untick one person, change another's department, tick the other-site person; press "Add n".
Run the import again for the same site.
cases.expected: step 1 the chip reads the site owner with "site owner", a searched person can be added and removed; step 2 the line counts people, managers and levels; step 3 the counts add up to the total, people under a department owner carry that department (an area owner's team carries the area too), the directory label fills gaps blind to case, disabled / guest / no-mailbox / office-elsewhere accounts are unticked with a red or amber chip and hidden until the toggle, the other-site person is unticked with an "on <site>" chip; step 4 the ticked people appear on Users as users of the site with the chosen departments, the moved person now shows the new site, the result names the access group's members added; step 5 everyone just added reads "already here" and the button is disabled with 0 to add

journeys.title: Journey 1 — Raising and following a report

cases.title: Withdraw my own report
cases.journey: Journey 1 — Raising and following a report
cases.preconditions: a report you raised that is still new or triaged
steps: Open the ? button → My reports.
On your open report click "Withdraw…"; give a reason; confirm.
As a super admin open Settings → Issues and find it.
cases.expected: the report's status reads Withdrawn with your reason on its thread; the Withdraw link shows only on your own open reports (never on one in progress, fixed or closed); the admin list shows it under Withdrawn and the PDF export carries the status
